title: Chicken breast, grilled with sauce, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken breast is a lean source of protein often grilled with a variety of sauces. Grilling retains most nutrients while the lack of skin reduces saturated fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast provides more protein per 100 g than most other meat cuts.
Grilling creates a distinctive flavor through Maillard reactions.
Sauces can be tomato‑based, yogurt‑based, honey‑glazed, or soy‑based, altering the taste profile.
Chicken is one of the oldest domesticated animals, kept for over 8,000 years.
When properly cooked, the breast stays juicy despite being skin‑less.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving of skinless chicken breast contains about 31 g of complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Without skin, the breast has less than 3 g of fat per 100 g, most of which are polyunsaturated.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones, immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Approximately 165 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may contain Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people can be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium in sauces
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain high salt; monitor sodium intake if needed.

items.title: Potential carcinogen formation
items.content: Excessive charring can produce heterocyclic amines; avoid burning the meat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the grilled breast hot as a main dish, slice it for salads, add to sandwiches, or incorporate into pasta dishes. Sauces can be served on the side or drizzled over the meat just before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a vacuum‑sealed bag for up to 9 months. Thaw in the fridge, and cooked leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 3 days.
